title: Grilled Beef & Lamb Feta Burgers
imagePrompt: A thick, hand-formed burger sits on a toasted brioche bun, its exterior deeply browned with charred grill marks and a few crisped edges where lamb fat rendered and caught the flame. The cut interior is juicy and rosy-brown, shot through with small white pockets of feta that have softened into creamy, slightly melted seams rather than dissolving into the meat. A thick smear of pale tzatziki clings to both bun halves, with dark-green arugula wilting slightly against the hot patty, a ruby slice of tomato, thin translucent rings of red onion, and a glossy yellow-green pepperoncini leaning off the side. Juices bead at the base of the patty and soak faintly into the bottom bun.
subtitle: Half lamb, half beef, gently folded with crumbled feta and grilled over direct heat until crusty outside and juicy within.

ingredients.heading: Ingredients
ingredients.note: Keep the meat cold right up until you mix — cold meat folds cleanly and stays loose.
items: 1 lb ground lamb (80–85% lean)
1 lb ground beef (80/20 preferred)
4 oz feta cheese, crumbled
3 cloves garlic, finely grated
2 tsp kosher salt
1½ tsp black pepper, freshly ground
1 tsp dried oregano
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 tsp ground cumin (optional but recommended)
1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (optional)
6 brioche or ciabatta buns, toasted
Tzatziki, for spreading
Sliced tomato
Red onion, thinly sliced
Arugula or butter lettuce
Roasted red peppers (optional)
Pickled pepperoncini (optional)
Good olive oil, for finishing
ingredients.callout: Restraint is the recipe: Fold the mixture like cookie dough, not bread dough. Overworking binds the proteins and gives you a dense, springy, sausage-like burger.

substitutes: Soy sauce + a dash of vinegar
Homemade — see the tzatziki recipe card

body.html: Beef brings richness, lamb brings earthiness, and the feta melts into little salty pockets throughout. This is a burger where restraint pays off — the goal is distinct pockets of cheese in loose, tender meat, not a uniform paste.

items: Mise en place — grate garlic, crumble feta, chop parsley, keep the meat cold
Blend the dry seasonings first so they distribute evenly
Spread and fold the meat 8–12 gentle times — no kneading
Form loose patties with a thumb dent in the center
Chill 20–30 minutes so they hold together on the grill
Grill over direct heat, flipping exactly once
Rest 5 minutes, then build on toasted buns with tzatziki

body.html: The one mistake to avoid: Overmixing. Stop folding the second everything looks evenly distributed.

slides.title: Mise en Place
slides.checkboxLabel: Everything prepped, meat still cold from the fridge

items: Finely grate the 3 cloves garlic and crumble the 4 oz feta.
Chop 1 tbsp parsley and measure 1 tbsp Worcestershire.
Slice tomato and red onion, wash the greens, and set out tzatziki and buns.
Leave the lamb and beef in the refrigerator until the moment you mix.
Have ready: a large bowl or sheet pan, a clear spot in the fridge for the formed patties, an instant-read thermometer, tongs, and a paper towel plus oil for the grates.

body.html: Keep everything cold. Don't let the meat sit out for 30 minutes while you prep — cold fat stays in distinct pieces and the mixture is far easier to handle.

slides.title: Blend the Seasonings
slides.checkboxLabel: Dry seasonings combined in a small bowl

items: In a small bowl, stir together the salt, pepper, oregano, smoked paprika, and cumin.
Set it beside the bowl you'll mix the meat in.

body.html: Why bother: Pre-blending lets you season evenly in one scattering pass instead of chasing pockets of salt around with extra mixing.

slides.title: Spread & Fold — Don't Knead
slides.checkboxLabel: Folded 8–12 times, feta still in visible pockets

items: Gently spread the beef and lamb into a shallow layer in a large bowl or on a sheet pan — don't dump it in one pile.
Scatter the garlic, Worcestershire, seasoning blend, parsley, and feta evenly over the surface.
Using your fingertips: lift from the bottom, fold over, rotate the bowl. Repeat.
8–12 gentle folds is usually enough.
Stop the moment everything looks evenly distributed.

body.html: Think cookie dough, not bread dough. Squeezing and kneading binds the proteins and gives you a dense, springy, sausage-like texture.

slides.title: Form the Patties
slides.checkboxLabel: 6 loose patties, ¾–1 inch thick, thumb dent in each

items: Divide the mixture into 6 equal portions (or 8 for smaller burgers).
Roll each portion just enough to hold together.
Flatten gently to ¾–1 inch thick and about ½ inch wider than your bun.
Press a shallow ¼-inch thumb dent into the center of each patty.
Do not compress them hard.

body.html: Loose patties = juicy burgers. The thumb dent keeps them from puffing into meatballs, and the extra width accounts for shrinkage.

items: Arrange the patties on a plate or sheet pan in a single layer.
Refrigerate 20–30 minutes.
Use the time to heat and clean the grill.

body.html: Why chill: Firmed-up fat holds the loose patties together when they hit the hot grates.

slides.title: Heat & Prep the Grill
slides.checkboxLabel: Grill at 425–450°F, grates clean and oiled

items: Preheat the grill to medium-high, around 425–450°F.
Clean the grates well — scrape them while hot.
Lightly oil the grates with a paper towel held in tongs.
Keep a cooler zone available for flare-ups.

body.html: Watch for flare-ups. Lamb fat ignites quickly. If flames climb, move the burgers to the cooler zone for a minute rather than letting them char.

slides.title: Grill — Leave Them Alone
slides.checkboxLabel: First side 4–5 min, released cleanly, flipped once

items: Place the burgers over direct heat.
Once they hit the grill: no pressing, no moving, no flattening.
After about 4–5 minutes they should release easily. If they stick, they aren't ready.
Flip once. Cook another 3–5 minutes, depending on thickness.

body.html: Never press with the spatula. You're squeezing flavorful juices into the fire, and every extra flip costs you crust.

slides.title: Temp & Rest
slides.checkboxLabel: Pulled at target temp, rested 5 minutes

measurements.qty: 145°F (less commonly recommended for mixed ground meats)

items: Use an instant-read thermometer — it's the only reliable guide for ground meat.
145°F is medium, though less commonly recommended for mixed ground meats.
155–160°F lands juicy and well-cooked; 160°F is the recommended safety minimum for ground meat.
Pull them 2–3°F before your target — they keep rising slightly as they rest.
Rest the burgers 5 minutes before building.

body.html: Resting isn't optional. Five minutes lets the juices redistribute instead of running out onto the plate the second you bite in.

slides.title: Build & Serve
slides.checkboxLabel: Buns toasted, burgers built and served

items: Toast the buns on the grill.
Spread tzatziki on both halves.
Layer: arugula, burger, tomato, red onion, pepperoncini.
Finish with a drizzle of good olive oil and a pinch of fresh parsley or oregano.

body.html: You're looking for: a crisp, well-browned exterior and a juicy, tender interior — rich from the beef, earthy from the lamb, with salty pockets of feta throughout and none of the heaviness.
